name: Natu Kodi Pulusu
subtitle: country chicken in a thin tamarind gravy, cooked long enough to matter

ingredients.note: free-range or older bird if you can, it is the point of the dish

prepNotes: Pulusu means sour. The tamarind is not a background note, it is the dish.
Country chicken is tougher and better flavoured than broiler. If you use broiler, cut the cooking time by half.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil until deep brown. Add the curry leaves and dried chillies.
Add the chicken, turmeric and coriander powder and fry on high until the pieces colour, 8 minutes.
Add the tomato and cook until it breaks down completely.
Strain in the tamarind water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 40 minutes until the chicken is tender.
steps.tip: It should stay thin. This is a gravy for pouring over rice, not for coating it.

steps.text: Season and rest 10 minutes. The sourness rounds out as it stands.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. The tamarind keeps it stable. Reheat to a full simmer.
